title: Boston’s foodie hot list is here!
text:
It’s Monday, Boston.

🥧 On your marks … Get set … BAKE! Bake Club Boston’s sweet treat meet-up literally sells out like hotcakes. So they set aside a handful of spots to its great pie off on June 27 just for B-Siders. Translation: Grab your tickets ASAP!

👀 What’s on tap today:

Hello, 3 a.m. last calls!

Wet weather woes

SMH, Google Maps

Up first…

BEST OF THE BEST

The ultimate treat yo’self guide

Image: Anthony Adamick. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

The Globe literally ate with this list. Enter: “Best of the Best,” a.k.a. the Boston Globe’s guide to the greatest restaurants, shopping, events, and more around Boston. From bagels to breweries, all 300 of these spots were handpicked by journalists and trusted correspondents.

Here are some of our main takeaways:

🍦Cambridge’s ice cream game is ELITE. With beloved creameries like Honeycomb, Christina’s, Toscanini’s, and New City, it’s no surprise that most of the Globe’s ice cream picks have Cambridge digs. But more under-the-radar spots like Forge Baking Co. in Somerville, Delini Gelato in Roxbury, and The Ice Creamsmith in Dorchester, still got some love.

☕ Boston runs on more than just Dunkin’. Between coffee legends like George Howell, Caffe Vitoria, and 1369 Coffee House, we already know the region brews a mean cup. And plenty of newer cafes are making a splash, like Yego Coffee in Somerville and Little Wolf, a North Shore staple that just opened in Seaport last year.

🧁 These bake shops are B-Side Certified. Kelly LOVES the chocolate brioche from Michette, half moons from Lyndell’s, egg tarts from Ho Yuen, and pretty much every baklava from Yafa. Plus, don’t forget to go to Sofra and get Emily’s faves like the date turmeric cinnamon and almond rose cake.

🤑 These sub-$25 meals are no joke. Did you know there’s still a breakfast sandwich for under $5? Neither did we *adds Evergreen in JP to our Beli*. That might be the best deal we saw on this list, but these recs feature any and every cuisine you’re in the mood for, from baba ghanoush at Amba to arepas from Viva Mi Arepa.

🛍️ Our thrifting scene is small but mighty. We all know of Garment District, Goodwill, and SoWa … which BTW, did make the “Best of the Best.” But if you’re looking for niche finds, you’ll probably have luck at Blue Bandana Relics in Somerville, which gives Maine cabin vibes, and 40 South St. in JP for ’70s statement pieces. Another hidden gem: The Thrift Shop of Boston in Roslindale for clothes, kitchenware, vinyl, and the works.

🙌 Want more? You can go through all 25+ lists here.

ADVERTISEMENT

TOGETHER WITH CAMBRIDGE TASTE

Social life feeling stale? Try this.

🍷 35+ reasons to camp out at University Park on June 17. Cambridge Taste is back with over 35 local restaurants sampling everything from sushi to wine to summer cocktails. Expect bites from Wusong Road’s innovative Asian cuisine, Barcelona Wine Bar’s Spanish small plates, Sumiao Hunan Kitchen’s fiery Hunan classics, plus Gufo’s handmade pasta, Fuji at Kendall’s fresh sashimi, Hourly Oyster’s raw bar, and so much more. All-inclusive tickets support local nonprofits. Get yours here.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: Gretchen Ertl for The Boston Globe.

🍻 We’re one step closer to 3 a.m. PBRs, people! Remember that 3 a.m. last call proposal? House lawmakers unanimously approved it. The goal is two-fold: to cash in on the tourist boom this summer, and as a test to see what a last-call extension would look like. So what now? If it passes the Senate, cities and towns can opt to extend one hour past closing, from June 8 through July 31. They can also set their rules about which businesses can participate and designate public consumption zones. But bartenders are skeptical of how this will play out …

☔ This weekend weather is giving us 2025 flashbacks. In classic Boston fashion, we’re seeing gorgina weekdays and buckets of rain on the weekends. And it’s been going on like this for 13 weeks … in a ROW. Why? 1. A ~wavy~ jet stream bringing colder air from the north. And 2. The recent heat created more moisture in the atmosphere. So … will we see a dry June weekend? Probably … Hopefully … at least once?

🚗 Park in this lot lawn for the World Cup. We remember this drill from the Eras Tour all too well … With FIFA selling parking passes at $175 a pop, some local residents are offering their own lawns as alternatives. This practice is technically banned in Foxborough, but being only a mile away, some Walpole locals are taking full advantage of applying for stadium event licenses. One man plans to have 26 spots, priced at $100 per car. For all seven games, he could make more than $18,000!

🤩 Two hot new bombshells (hangouts) entered the villa (Boston). The Lawn on D just got a fresh green facelift and gave itself a new name, The Grove. Think: Lush greenery, cabanas, live music, and a menu packing poké bowls, watermelon frosés, and s’mores martinis. In the mood for carbs on the go? Curb your pasta cravings FAST at the Presto Pasta window in the North End. Just pick your pasta shape, sauce, and toppings, and voila!

THINGS TO DO

Weekday plans

Image: Craig F. Walker/The Boston Globe.

🤠 Giddy up to your next girl dinner. Hunter’s new cowgirl dinner deal is what dreams are made of: Steak frites + your choice of side salad = $30. Only available on Mondays!

🏌️ Make Wednesdays for the women. Five Iron Golf is celebrating Women’s Golf Month with up to 90 minutes of free play for the ladies on Wednesdays all June.

💻 See if a four-day work week is worth it. That’s the topic of discussion at this Binge Thinking event on June 10, where an expert shares what’s really happening inside companies trying it.

🌹 Bask among the blooms. The Kelleher Rose Garden is *this close* to peak bloom. Perfect timing for its annual Rose Garden picnic party on June 10 — yes it’s free!

🏳️‍🌈 Werk it at the market. The Brighton Bazaar is throwing its first-ever LGBTQ+ themed Big Gay Bazaar on June 11. Expect drag, a Lady Gaga Tribute, 100+ curated LGBTQ+ vendors, and more!

🌴 Outwit, outplay, outlast. Yes, we’re talking about Survivor Aeronaut on June 12, where you and your pals can play epic Survivor-style challenges and puzzles (all over a beer, ofc).

⚽ Practice your olé, olé, olés. Friendly reminder that the FIFA Fan Festival kicks off June 12 at City Hall Plaza, a prime spot for catching a match.

🍸 Get a taste of these STUNNING spring cocktails.* 89 Charles’ intimate cocktail lounge just unveiled fresh martinis, seasonal sips, and zero-proof options alongside elevated bar bites. It’s the kind of place you’ll keep coming back to. Reserve here.

*This listing is presented in partnership with 89 Charles.

COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT

⚽ The World Cup has arrived. Here’s where to watch.

The World Cup is in Boston, and Fenway FC is your headquarters until the Final on July 19. Time Out Market Boston and Cisco Brewers are streaming every match — group stage, knockouts, all of it — and they’re staying open late because soccer waits for no one.

Catch the action on big screens inside and out on The Green at 401 Park. Or if coastal New England vibes are more your speed, post up in Cisco’s beer garden for cold craft pours and mouthwatering bites. When you’re ready for dinner, MIDA’s Boylston Street patio, bartaco, Shy Bird’s dog-friendly terrace, and The Citizen’s sidewalk seats put you right in the thick of it. Don’t be shy, pull up a chair in The Fenway for the full 90!

ONE LAST THING

A DoorDash dilemma

Image: AP Photo/David Zalubowski. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

What would you do if 36 lunches showed up on your front porch? Well, this woman — and the rats that would sniff it out — had been getting misplaced deliveries for YEARS (literally everything from ice cream cake to a McDonald’s Coke).

Why, you may ask? Frumie L. Burns wrote for Brookline News how her address is nearly the same as Brigham and Women’s Hospital. But one was Brookline and the other was Boston. To make it worse, they were less than one mile away from each other. And Google Maps never got it right.

Frumie and her husband tried their best to redirect delivery drivers to the hospital. In many cases, the two would quickly bring it over themselves, especially if it was flowers.

It got so bad that the couple even tried to change their address officially. But finally, Frumie’s husband wrote a lengthy complaint to Google Maps and DoorDash … and so far, it’s been a few weeks without a wrong delivery. Fingers crossed!

— Written by Kelly Chan and Emily Schario

🥤 Thanks for reading! To all the BW nurses who never got their lunch order … it’s probably at Frumie’s.

💜 Special shoutout to today’s sponsor, Cambridge Taste, for supporting local journalism and giving us the gift of adult recess (and a social life) season after season.

🦞 The results are in: Wow, most of you got our pop quiz question right! The first (recorded) lobster roll was served at a Connecticut restaurant in the 1920s. “Lobster had the most extreme glow-up,” one of you said. She really did that.

title: Hot take: Europe is a weekend trip from Boston
text:
Happy Friday, Boston!

🍻🏀 Just in time for tip off … Time Out Market’s bar is back open, and they’re broadcasting EVERY March Madness game. The best part? You can try allll the new bites: pizza at Lala’s, wings at Ms. Cluck’s Deluxe, tacos at Taqueria el Barrio, and more. Seating is open, so show up early!

👀What’s on tap today:

Northeastern won grad szn

PorchFest porta-potties

Delivery for City Hall!

Up first…

TRAVEL

London Calling (for the weekend)

Video and gif: Emily Schario

Hot take: If you can sit in six hours of Cape traffic for a long weekend … you can sit on a six-hour transatlantic flight for one. At least that’s what I told myself when I found myself in this … “situation” last summer.

TikTok is currently obsessed with day trips across the pond … So I did what any curious journalist would do: I got on a red-eye flight to London last Wednesday and flew home Sunday morning.

Here’s what I learned:

😴 A morning power nap > a fitful night of plane sleep. Yes, do your best to get some in-flight shut eye, but from one girl in economy to another: Don’t bet on it. A solid two-hour post-flight hotel nap is enough to give you a second wind for the afternoon.

📍Say it with me now: I will NOT make any firm plans on day one. You’ll be running on caffeine and delusion, babe. Use it as your chance to get the lay of the land without the pressure to pay attention. For us, that meant snapping pics of the greatest hits: Buckingham Palace, Big Ben, Westminster Abbey. And then just … wandering. We stumbled into gorgeous bookstores, this buzzing food hall, and one of the city’s oldest fish-and-chips shops.

⚓ After day one … anchor your days. Pick one to two high-priority plans — the things you’d be genuinely sad to miss, ideally with reservations — and build around them. Friday’s anchors were lunch at Indian restaurant Dishoom and the splurge-worthy afternoon tea at the Ritz. Saturday’s anchors were the Tower of London and a matinee in the West End.

🚶 Fill the gaps with ~wandering-forward~ activities. Think: Exploring Notting Hill, snacking through Borough Market, and shopping in Marylebone — all of which can be stretched or cut short, depending on the vibe.

📝 Ask a local before you ask TikTok. If your FYP is pushing these viral chocolate strawberries at Borough Market … keep walking … to this flaky, buttery sausage roll from The Ginger Pig. Shoutout to the cheesemonger — your rec did not disappoint!

🪫 Accept that you’ll never quite fully recharge your battery. We lucked out with daylight savings (only a four-hour difference), but still felt it. A consistent bedtime routine will be your BFF.

✈️ JetBlue is *that girl* if you’re flying economy. Everyone got complimentary booze, they had all my plane comfort movies, functioning WiFi (!), and Dig Inn was an in-flight meal.

✅ Would I do it again? 100%. Would I choose it over the Cape if I saw a good flight deal? In a heartbeat.

ADVERTISEMENT

TOGETHER WITH FIDO PIZZA

Pizza for smart people

🧠🍻 You’ve been training for this your whole life (a.k.a. watching Jeopardy every night for as long as you can remember). FiDO Pizza hosts Geeks Who Drink Jeopardy! Bar League Trivia every Sunday at 3 p.m., where Daily Doubles, Final Jeopardy chaos, and competitive teams meet hot pizza and cold beer. Prizes are up for grabs and the full menu is available — including a gluten-friendly pizza crust (+$4) made with deglutinated wheat and baked in a shared oven. Grab your trivia team, reserve a table, and see if all that random knowledge pays off.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: Frazer Harrison/Getty

👩🏼‍🎓 Northeastern’s graduation is what dreams are made of. Translation: Hilary Duff will be its 2026 commencement speaker! For our non-millennial readers, Duff was a 2000s teen idol known for her starring role in Disney’s “Lizzie McGuire,” plus countless other shows and movies (she’s also gearing up for her first global headline tour in two decades!). Northeastern dropped the news in an Y2K-themed reel, complete with a sparkly flip phone and a “The Lizzie McGuire Movie” poster. Let’s just say, other schools were appropriately jealous. She’ll give her speech at Fenway Park on April 29.

🎸 Somerville’s PorchFest has a new addition to the lineup: TONS of porta-potties. The beloved DIY music festival that takes place on neighborhood porches returns May 9 with tons of great music … and “at least double” the porta-potties, a spokesperson said. This potty palooza is part of the festival’s beefed-up safety guardrails following some WILD crowds in 2024. Think: Banning performances on main streets and enlisting a group of volunteers. Plastic thrones aside … You can sign up to volunteer, perform, or host here!

🦞 Inflation is coming for Boston’s lobster rolls. Restaurateurs predict the price of lobster rolls will approach $50(!) this summer thanks to soaring business costs, inflation, and climate change. The uptick puts local businesses in a tough situation: Jack up prices, or leave the rolls off the menu entirely. Either way, they risk alienating regulars and tourists alike who expect to see the local staple on the menu. And with Boston’s banner summer of tourism coming up, many will have to decide soon.

🦆 The Duck Boat Challenge is BACK. On April 11, teams of ten will race against the clock to drag a 21,000-pound duck boat across the Common, a.k.a. The Duck Boat Challenge. Yes, it looks as wild as it sounds. The event debuted last year as a way to raise money for youth sports in Boston, and Curry College football team took home the W (surprise, surprise). If you have $1,000 to blow, you can register here before March 27. Otherwise, spectating is free!

THINGS TO DO

Weekend plans

Image courtesy of Bow Market Book Fair

😂 Watch comedians fight to the DEATH. Or … until they get kicked off stage. Tonight at The Rockwell, local comics will compete in a standup battle judged by the audience until one remains.

📚 Stay booked and busy. It’s easy at Bow Market’s Book Fair on March 21! On the docket: Bookseller pop-ups, author signings and panels, crafting workshops, and WAY more.

🥵 Heat up the dance floor. This “Heated Rivalry” queer dance party and drag show at Nathálie Wine Bar on March 21 may be hockey-themed, but trust us, there will be nothing icy about it.

🌈 Celebrate the festival of colors. A.k.a. Holi! Head to Adams Park on March 21 for Holi Mela 2026, with food, dancing, and tons of color. Seriously: Don’t wear anything you don’t want to turn rainbow.

🪩 Dance the night away (but be home by midnight). You can truly have it all at High Street Place’s Home By Midnight bash on March 21.

🧶 Get hooked on fiber arts. Get it? Boston Public Market’s Fiber Fest on March 21 and 22 features local pop-up vendors and fiber arts workshops, like this adorable denim patch class!

👖 Thrift your new spring wardrobe. Select Markets is back with a springy thrift market at the Revere Hotel on March 21 and 22. Think: 70+ vendors, $10 piles, temporary tattoos, and tooth gems.

🛍️ Shop ‘til you drop in the Fenway. Time Out and Mighty Squirrel Brewery are both hosting vendor markets in the neighborhood this weekend with oodles of local art, vintage, vinyl, and more!

COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT

Art, food, and magic under the Cyclorama dome.

🎨 Boston is gearing up for a one-night culinary experience featuring four legendary Boston chefs: Lydia Shire, Gordon Hamersley, Jody Adams, and Joanne Chang. They’re collaborating on Dinner Under the Dome, a four-course dinner created exclusively for this evening, woven together with live art activations by Boston Center for the Arts artists. Proceeds support BCA and its resident artists. Reserve here.

ONE LAST THING

Delivery for City Hall!

Images courtesy of Alex Alex

If you see a pile of trash on City Hall Plaza, it’s probably Alex Alex. The Dorchester resident has gone viral on social media for collecting pieces of broken city infrastructure like bus signs and traffic cones, loading them in a cart, and lugging them to City Hall.

Alex, who ran a longshot campaign for mayor last fall, said his actions are about bringing the city’s inaction and misallocation of resources to light. The idea came about after his concerns were brushed off by city officials (though they seem to disagree).

So far, he’s picked up over 5,000 pounds of trash and racked up the views on Instagram, where his mission is resonating with viewers. “I’m not invited to these rooms where policies are being made … but what I can do is point out infrastructure that’s physically visible to everybody,” he told Boston.com.

— Written by Gia Orsino and Emily Schario

🚧 Thanks for reading! Say what you will, but five miles with 200 pounds of trash is DEDICATION.

💜 Special shoutout to today’s sponsor, FiDO Pizza, for supporting local journalism and giving us all a tasty neighborhood spot to keep coming back to.

👃 The results are in: 45% of readers said neti pots and nasal spray are their go-to allergy season hacks. One reader said: “Hiding in a hole until the forbidden yellow dust is gone!” That’s one way to do it!

title: The MBTA’s Gilmore Girls era
text:
Happy Friday, Boston!

⛴️ Set your alarms for a free ferry! Save the Harbor is dropping tickets at midnight on Sept. 13 for a free roundtrip ride to Spectacle Island on Oct. 4. Woo!

🥨 Party like it’s Oktober. We’re kicking off Oktoberfest season with Sam Adams Boston Brewery and Sam Adams Downtown Taproom! Tune into Saturday’s B-Side Member newsletter to snag a free pair of tickets — we’ve got two pairs for each event! Didn’t win? The first 50 Members can take 20% off.

Want in? Start a Membership for 50% off here. You just have to be the first to email us according to the directions. Prost!

👀 What’s on tap today:

Foliage forecast

The ultimate workout weekend

Boston’s karaoke king

Up first…

TRAVEL

$1 fall day trips make us holla

Image: John Tlumacki/The Boston Globe. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

Friendly reminder for our fellow Type A baddies: Commuter rail weekend passes are just $10, AND if you’re a monthly pass holder, you can bring one companion on weekend trips for just $1 each way through November (thanks, Gov. Healey!).

So we talked to our pals, our co-workers, and our team to map out four weekend-worthy autumnal adventures for you and bestie. Here’s where we’d go:

🧙 Salem, Mass.: I mean … duh. But fair warning: It’s gonna be packed come October. So head up this month to beat the spooky rush. Our game plan:

Fuel up at A&J King Artisan Bakers with fresh pastries and coffee.

Hit up the spooky staples like the “Bewitched” statue, the Ropes Mansion, the Witch House, and The House of the Seven Gables.

Explore the Peabody Essex Museum — it covers everything from witch trials to nature and science. This studio glass exhibit looks SICK.

Shop the city’s Haunted Happenings Marketplace for spooky trinkets and treats.

Cap off the night with freshly-baked cookies from Goodnight Fatty (obv).

🍎 Ayer + Harvard, Mass.: These quaint towns nestled in Nashoba Valley are loaded with rolling hills, fabulous foliage, and sweet treats galore. Our dream date looks something like this:

Grab a fresh apple fritter and coffee from Adams Donut Shop.

Fill a bag with fresh-picked apples at Doe Orchards.

Leaf peep along the Nashua River Rail Trail — you can walk or BYOB (bring your own bike!).

Step inside Amos Bronson Alcott’s utopian experiment at the Fruitlands Museum.

🍁 Ipswich, Mass.: You might not think beach + fall adds up to an ideal autumn outing. But this itinerary might change your tune:

Grab coffee and a breakfast sammie from Sandpiper Bakery.

Dig for vintage treasure at AnnTiques.

Pretend Castle Hill on the Crane Estate is your mansion for the day.

Enjoy an autumnal stroll along the gorgeous Crane Beach (just make sure to grab a pass!).

Pick apples, sip local wine, and say hi to cutie farm animals at Russell Orchards.

🧖 Newburyport, Mass.: She’s the queen of the downtown bop and shop. But Newburyport (and the surrounding area) is home to plenty of cozy fall excursions that go beyond the usual shmy:

Experience Skog & Stone Sauna Co.’s Finnish-style sauna on the beach on Plum Island.

Grab coffee and pastries at Middle Street Foods.

Uber to Cider Hill Farm (technically in Amesbury) for apple picking and cider doughnuts.

Take a fall hot girl walk through Maudslay State Park for epic leaf-peeping.

ADVERTISEMENT

TOGETHER WITH SNOWBOUND EXPO

“Isn’t it a little early to be thinking about snow?”

❄️🎿 Respectfully, no. Snowbound Expo is already getting ready to bring the snow-sport community together Nov. 14–15 at Mohegan Sun. Come shop gear, get inspired by Olympians and athletes, watch some seriously unhinged tricks at the Rail Jam, and catch 60 looks on the Alpine runway. Then stick around for the Ice Bar and Saturday’s Après Party After Hours. For a limited time only, Early-Bird tickets are 50% off with code BSIDE.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe.

🍁 This foliage season is about to HIT. At least, compared to years past. Globe meteorologist Ken Mahan is expecting a good ol’, classic, vibrant New England fall with all the reds, oranges, and yellows of your dreams. We can thank those snowy winter days and our wet July for the bright hues. Pencil in your leaf-peeping trips for mid- to late October for peak season, but note: coastal areas will probs be the last to peak. Bonus: If we get good rain this month, we’ll be set for a loooooooong leaf-peeping season.

✍️ Lindsay Clancy’s attorney is doing the most to avoid a retrial. Kevin Reddington renewed a motion asking the judge to reconsider Clancy’s requests for a not-guilty finding, which can be granted when there’s not enough evidence to convict. He’s also trying to get her case dismissed entirely on double jeopardy grounds … except hung-jury mistrials typically don’t count toward double jeopardy. He argued that the judge could’ve done more about the lone holdout juror (who another juror called out for “disgusting” behavior during deliberations).

🎹 The BPL’s newest resource: pianos! Four BPL locations are rolling out pianos for children and teens to learn the keys fo’ free through the Lang Lang Foundation’s Keys of Inspiration Program. Fun fact: The BPL is the first U.S. library system to be part of it. The program typically partners with school districts, but is now expanding to community centers and libraries, starting with Boston and London. Folks will be able to tickle six new ivories total (plus tablets and learning apps) across the Grove Hall, Hyde Park, Lower Mills, and Central branches.

🏋️ Boston’s workout lineup is STACKED this weekend. You’ve got three options on Sept. 12: 1. Seaport’s Sweatapalooza, a free outdoor fitness festival with three workouts, pop-ups, and giveaways. 2. Boston Landing’s Community Fit Fest (also free!) with classes, wellness activations, and more. And 3. Seaav’s Make Waves Movement class at Tall Ship. Then wind down with a walking club collab in Seaport on Sept. 13, where the first 25 people to check in will get a Lululemon accessory.

THINGS TO DO

Weekend plans

🍺 Put on your lederhosen! It’s time to get into the Oktoberfest spirit with lagers, steinholding contests, and live music at Remnant from Sept. 11-13 or Long Live Roxbury on Sept. 12.

🛍️ Snag the South End’s best deals. All your fave local businesses (think: Covet, Parkside Bookshop, and Clay Lounge) are rolling out sweet deals for the South End Sidewalk Sale from Sept. 11-13. Here’s the map!

🧶 Go all in on your fiber arts obsession. First, join the Sept. 11 kickoff party and sip-and-stitch night at Boston Fiber Company. Then spend the weekend at Boston Fiber Fest, ft. classes on knitting, mending, and more.

🧑‍🦲 Meet Boston’s baldest baddies. Whether you’ve got a chrome dome or are just an ally, join the Bald Meetup at High Street Place on Sept. 12. Expect comedy, giveaways, and even cash prizes for anyone who shaves their head at the event.

🥟 Eat all the dumplings your heart desires. Saturday’s challenge: You v. Mei Mei Dumplings’ AYCE dumpling buffet on Sept. 12. Feast on options like lemongrass pork, cheeseburger, and cheddar scallion potato.

💃 Put on your dancing shoes. Keep grooving nonstop performances at the East Boston Latin Music Dance Festival on Sept. 12. Bonus: There’ll be tons of free tastings from Eastie’s restaurants like La Hacienda and Los Alebrijes.

🥃 Bottoms up for rum o’clock! The Caribbean Rum & Food Festival on Sept. 12 will have rum punch (included with your ticket!), cocktails, authentic nibbles, entertainment, and crafts. Get tickets here!

🙌 Support your local AAPI makers. The Made in Boston Festival is BACK. Browse tons of AAPI vendors selling food, handmade goods, and more at Arts for the Armory on Sept. 13.

ONE LAST THING

Boston’s karaoke king

Image: Lane Turner/The Boston Globe. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

PSA: You can get free front row seats to an Olivia Rodrigo concert! Well, sort of …

Meet Steven Arcieri (@normalsteven on TikTok), a local karaoke legend at SideBar who, let’s just say, sings like his life depends on it. He’s performed everything from “I Write Sins Not Tragedies” by Panic! At the Disco to “Vroom Vroom” by Charli XCX — and the man doesn’t miss a beat (though we can’t say he’s exactly on key).

And now, he’s hitting the big stage: On Sept. 12 at 6:30 p.m., Steven’s singing Olivia’s *entire* new album at the Parkman Bandstand on the Common. In fact, he’s aptly advertising it as, “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Steven So in Love.” Bonus: It’s free!

Plus, you can even get a Cameo from him that will help fund him getting his own Olivia Rodrigo concert ticket.

— Written by Kelly Chan and Emily Schario

🫣 Thanks for reading! Social anxiety fears him.

💜 Special shoutout to today’s sponsor, Snowbound Expo, for supporting local journalism and already getting us hyped for winter 2026.

⚡ The results are in: 79% of B-Siders are anti-large data centers. One reader said, “I prefer drinking water over Gemini writing a stupid email for me, thanks.” Louder for the people in the back!

title: Apple cider doughnut-maxxing
text:
Happy Friday, Boston!

🚴 OK, now THIS is a life hack we need: We just learned you can get this sick Bluebikes key fob to unlock a bike (instead of fumbling through the app). Bonus: You can pick one up for FREE at the BPL!

📲 Pssst! We’d really like to hear what you think! The Brief is a new local daily news app designed for younger audiences. What you’ll find: 10 important stories with a clear ending — no infinite scrolling. Sign up here to join the beta!

🥳 And everyone say HBD to Members Patti and Riley Davis! Ah yes, a Bluebikes key fob and a doomscroll-free news app — just what you asked for!

👀 What’s on tap today:

Nor’easter news

Amtrak fall sale

Love Is Blind Boston

Up first…

OUT & ABOUT

Fall-maxx, no car required

Image: Wendy Maeda/The Boston Globe. Illustration: Emily Schario.

You see it now: Your bestie with a car is taking performative IG pics at an apple orchard an hour outside the city. Meanwhile, you’re seething with jealousy from your tiny Boston apartment.

Don’t fret, sweet B-Sider. We’ve got ways to fall-maxx around the city, no car required.

Here’s the plan:

🍎 Sip on boozy apples at Downeast Cider House. Cream puff. Apple pie. Pumpkin. That’s just a taste of the many cider flavors you might find on tap in Downeast’s Eastie taproom. You can build your own tasting flight from their rotating lineup, or grab a full pour in their outdoor cider garden. Bonus: Make it a full outing with one of their pottery workshop nights this weekend. <3

🍩 Chow down on the best apple cider doughnut in town. Hot take: The cider doughnuts from Red Apple Farm at the Boston Public Market > any apple cider doughnut we’ve tried outside the city. YUP. They’re piping hot, adorably mini, and earned a crucial endorsement: Alex Schwartz, creator of the New England Cider Donut Map, said, “they have doughnut-making down to a science.” Say less.

🪦 Get spooked by Boston’s Puritan history. Who knew death could be … fun? At least that’s how we felt after hopping on a Boston By Foot tour to explore Roxbury’s Eliot Burying Ground (you can also tour the Dorchester North). It’s the perfect mix of Puritan history in a spooky setting (also, the tombstones are gorgeous?). But for full-on spook, catch their Beacon Hill with a BOO! tour to uncover the murder and mayhem lurking beneath the neighborhood …

🎃 Pick the prettiest pumpkin in all the patch at Allandale Farm. OK, this may not be a traditional pumpkin patch. But, this MBTA-accessible farm might be the closest thing to a fall farm moment without a drive. They just laid out this gorgeous plot of pumpkins and squash, along with their usual lineup of fresh farm produce and flowers.

🛶 Paddle in the glow of the fall moon. Part wildlife/history tour, part outdoor adventure, Paddle Boston’s moonlight tour along the Charles is a chill, 2-3-mile group paddle that’s sure to put you in your autumn feels. But frankly, a solo paddle might be our favorite way to leaf peep.

🍁 Take in the trees with a foliage walk at Mount Auburn Cemetery. You already know we’re huge fans of this gorgina landscaped cemetery in Cambridge, and fall is where she really shines. Hop on one of their guided foliage walks to see the cemetery’s most colorful trees. Our only non-negotiable: Climb Washington Tower for panoramic views of Boston and beyond.

ADVERTISEMENT

TOGETHER WITH ADOBE

New semester, new coping mechanism 📚

🎓✨ Instead of buying another planner you’ll abandon by October, try something actually useful. Adobe’s Student Spaces in Acrobat is now available (for free!) with tools to help you study smarter, including custom study guides, video and audio summaries, citation generation, and handwritten-note conversion. It can even help review your resume and prep for interviews. Basically, one less thing to panic about.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: Craig F. Walker/The Boston Globe

🌀 Get ready to rumble with a rare fall nor’easter. The wind’s a howlin’, the sky’s a stormin’, and Emily’s flight is … still set for takeoff (for now). 4-6 inches of rain, 50-55 mph winds, coastal flooding, and scattered power outages are all possibilities as this storm barrels through New England, starting around 5 p.m. today and lingering into at least Sunday. So hunker down and queue up this list of new shows and movies to watch. Keep an eye on the storm’s latest here.

😷 A small lesbian bar in Western Mass. broke the internet. And after reading this Globe magazine piece, we totally get why. Long story short: Last Ditch Bar in Greenfield needed to attract more biz, so it announced it was relaxing its very strict masking requirements from seven nights a week to six, with Saturday being mask optional. Then all hell broke loose in ways you’d never predict. Ex: One commenter suggested the bar was trying to “kill disabled people in the name of your own leisure and convenience.” Oh!

🧙 All aboard, witches. We’re going to Salem. The MBTA and Keolis announced they’ll be operating extra commuter rail trains to and from Salem every weekend in October. Woo! The bonus trains will operate during peak times on the Newburyport/Rockport Commuter Rail Line to accommodate folks heading up for Salem’s Haunted Happenings events. And these trains are necessary, as 111,000+ passengers rode the train to Salem during October weekends in 2025.

🚂 Amtrak’s fall sale = your excuse to use some PTO. The leaves aren’t the only things falling rn. Enter: Amtrak’s Falling Fares Sale, where travelers can get at least 25% off travel almost anywhere in the country (we’re looking at you, Northeast Regional!). Your job: Book by Sept. 30 for travel between Oct. 14 and Dec. 17 — just pay attention to these blackout dates and restrictions. Heads up: We saw some one-ways to NYC for as low as $21!

COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT

💍 Forget shopping for jewelry. Make it instead.

The Jewelry Bar in Canton, Mass. is an interactive space where you create something uniquely yours. The options are endless: custom charms, permanent jewelry, beaded designs, engraved pieces, lip gloss. It’s part workshop, part social experience, and frankly, part therapy. Whether you’re looking for some weeknight R&R or need a bachelorette outing, The Jewelry Bar can turn a few hours of jewelry making into exactly what YOU need. Learn more here!

THINGS TO DO

Weekend plans

🍺 Witness your first stein showdown. High Street Place’s free Fall Fest is bringing seasonal bites and brews, live music, lawn games, and a stein-holding competition to the food hall on Sept. 26.

🎨 See Chinatown through a new lens. Sept. 26 is the city’s free Experience Chinatown festival where you can watch live performances, and support AAPI businesses.

🧣 Go secondhand for your fall wardrobe update. Covet is blessing Boston baddies with 20% off regular items and 10% off luxury pieces at its Beacon Hill store on Sept. 26 and 27.

🍕 Beat the Sunday scaries … with pizza and wine. PSA: Petula’s in Southie has the ultimate Sunday dinner deal: $55 for a choice of pizza plus a bottle of vino.

🦖 Spend a night at the museum. Sept. 27 = Adult Night at Science Park, where grownups can experience the Museum of Science after-hours at this adults-only night.

🥾 Snag the ultimate fall starter pack. Dunkin’ and L.L.Bean are teaming up for the collab heard ‘round New England: a merch and food pop-up at the Seaport L.L.Bean store on Sept. 27. Race you there!

🍂 Browse a cozy market for fall trinkets. Browse handmade jewelry, zines, vintage finds, and artisanal goods from local makers at Sunday’s Boston Hassle’s Autumn Makers Market at Cambridge Community Center on Sept. 27.

ONE LAST THING

Love Is Blind in Boston!

Image: Netflix. Illustration: Emily Schario.

THIS IS NOT A DRILL! “Love Is Blind: Boston” has a premiere date!!!!

You’ve seen the casting calls, heard the filming rumblings, and might’ve even spotted a gold goblet in the wild. But we can now confirm that the Boston season of the iconic Netflix series will officially air Oct. 14. AH!

In case you’ve been living under a rock: “Love Is Blind” is a show where a group of single men and women from the same metro area are separated into “pods” where they can only hear each other’s voices to get to know each other. They can only meet face-to-face after they’ve gotten engaged. And, generally, chaos ensues …

We’re still waiting on an official trailer, cast list, and the locations of where things were filmed. But trust, as soon as we know more, we’ll be all over it …

— Written by Emily Schario

title: The flirtiest workout in Boston
text:
Happy Friday, Boston!

🍦 Get in loser, we’re going to Flour. They just added peach soft-serve to their menu, and we need a cone STAT!

🪩 Also … want in on Boston’s biggest party?. Boston magazine’s *iconic* Best of Boston soireé is July 22. Imagine: Free bites from 30 of Boston best restaurants, signature cocktails, and tons of swag. And we have two pairs of FREE tickets! Tune into Saturday’s Member newsletter to claim them!

👀 What’s on tap today:

Boston is bone-dry

Three grand openings

World Cup walk

Up first…

SUMMER FRIDAYS

Poetry, pickleball, and pasta

Image: Kayla Bartkowski for The Boston Globe. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

Bad news: It’s our first Tartan Army-free weekend. Good news: We’ve filled your weekend with events that will keep the party going.

Here’s what’s going down:

💃 Bust a move in Camberville. Calling all party people: You can break it down with DJs and a light show at Cambridge’s annual city dance party on June 26. Then hit the floor at the Big Gay Dance Party in Union Square on June 27.

☁️ Get lost in the clouds. Introducing: “Better Angels,” the Triennial’s latest sick public art installation pop-up at Atlantic Wharf, featuring inflatable clouds, heavenly gates, and campy angels. Take a stroll June 26-28!

⛴️ Say ahoy to Spectacle Island! Translation: Ferry service officially resumes Saturday. Plus, you can ride it seven days a week, all summer long. Buy your tickets here.

🌆 Soak up some rooftop views. Grab your besties for this Truly rooftop summer kickoff party at MGM Music Hall on June 26. Expect snacks and drinks, a DJ, a 1987 pop-up, AND a custom patch station. Even better: There’s no cover. <3

🫰 Snap for the poets that know it. Join artists, writers, and educators at the Roxbury Poetry Festival on June 27 for a fabulous lineup of workshops, panels, and a poetry slam where one winner will land a book deal.

⚽ Bring the World Cup vibes to Boston proper. No need to hike to Foxborough. Instead, head to Ballers in the Seaport on June 27 to watch local Boston teams in the CNCPTS Cup (a.k.a. a 4 v. 4 soccer tournament). Then stick around for giveaways, custom jerseys, and skills challenges.

🏓 Meet your match on (and off) the court. Bring your sneakers (and your best banter) to Pickleball Social Club’s Singles Mixer on June 27. You’ll rotate between playing and mingling, switching up partners after short rounds. No paddle? No problem! They’ve got you covered.

🪩 Practice your “Super Trouper” routine. ‘Cause “Mamma Mia” is playing at Saguaro’s outdoor movie night on June 27. Free entry + food and bev specials + ABBA on repeat = our kind of Saturday night.

🍽️ Get drunk on drunken noodles. Chow down on all your Thai food faves (think: pork skewers and mango sticky rice) at Thai Taste on the Common on June 28.

🍝 Just go with the flow dough. A FREE pasta masterclass?! Sign us up. This is a guided sesh at SoWa Open Market on June 28, featuring hands-on practice, samples, and fresh pasta to take home with you.

ADVERTISEMENT

TOGETHER WITH MA250

The birthday party starts here

🎂🇺🇸 Turning 250 is a pretty big deal. Luckily, Massachusetts has been preparing for this moment for about two and a half centuries. To celebrate America’s milestone birthday, MA250 is bringing history to life through festivals, exhibits, performances, sporting events, and community celebrations across the state. See what’s happening near you and join the party.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: Craig F. Walker/The Boston Globe.

💦 Soooo … our wet weekends need to be wetter. We can’t believe we’re saying that either, but this is actually the city’s driest year on record. Boston has just under a foot of precipitation this year — nine inches less than average. And if the drought continues, we’re at risk of dry wells, brush fires, and fewer fall crops, which may require us to enforce *extensive* water bans on things like lawn maintenance. Right now, experts say we either need more consistent rain … or a tropical storm.

🍺 One hot girl walk with a side of pale ale, please! Translation: Roundhead Brewing is back bringing your fave traveling beer garden all around the city this summer. It’s slated to pop up at six parks through September, and will be open Friday to Sunday till 9 p.m. (heads up: opening hours vary each day). This is their last weekend in Copley Square Park; they’ll move to Menino Park in Charlestown next week. Cheers!

🎉 It’s a good day to be a shopper with a sweet tooth. ‘Cause there are three grand openings in town just for you: 1. Sweet Teez’s famous cakes are now available at a new brick-and-mortar in Dorchester on June 26. 2. Teso Life, an Asian lifestyle superstore with snacks, skincare products, and home goods, is open June 26. 3. Vivant Vintage’s new massive two-story hub in Allston opens for biz June 27.

COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT

An all-day Caribbean party

🌶️ Get ready for JerkFest, Boston’s spiciest event. It’s all going down on July 11 at Ohiri Field in Allston. Expect jerk dishes, local vendors, talented chefs, and live music to keep the energy going all day. Whether you’re a die-hard Caribbean foodie or just looking for a sunny Saturday outing, JerkFest is your spot. B-Side Members save $5 on Friday and Saturday tickets. Get tickets here!

ONE LAST THING

One hot Gillette walk

Image: Adobe. Illustration: Megan Le for The Boston Globe.

On today’s episode of “men walking really far distances,” we bring you Miles Howard, the founder of Walking City Trails.

Miles decided to walk from Boston to Gillette Boston Stadium the day of the Haiti v. Scotland match. After all, transit there was pricey, and it was *just* 17 miles away …

The scorching heat bogged him down the first few miles, but as he got closer to the stadium, he found himself rejuvenated by a group of Haitian fans, and was later joined by Scotsmen also traveling on foot (always a Scotland connection).

When they finally got to the stadium, they received a hero’s welcome (and a Narragansett tallboy) from the rest of the Tartan Army, boasting flags and singing loudly in classic Scottish fashion.

Oh, we almost forgot to mention … Miles didn’t even have a ticket to the game. But for him, coming together and celebrating on a game day > everything else. Awwww.

— Written by Kelly Chan and Emily Schario

🚶 Thanks for reading! The one guy that might actually walk 500 miles (for the Tartan Army).

💜 Special shoutout to today’s sponsor, MA250, for supporting local journalism and turning 250 years of history into surprisingly good weekend plans.

title: The best things to do around Boston this weekend
text:

Commuter rail chaos

New byChae matcha cafe

MEGA lobstah roll

Up first…

SUMMER FRIDAYS

Drag shows, desserts, and Dorchfest

Image: Erin Clark/The Boston Globe. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

Is “booked and busy” your middle name? It sure will be after adding all of these goodies to your social calendar this weekend.

Here’s what’s cookin’:

🎤 See that fried chicken guy in Southie. Your fave local comedian Joe Fenti (yes, the one who loves to drag the Seaport) will be performing standup at Castle Island Brewing on June 5.

🌈 Show your Pride at the MFA. Art-making, gallery talks, a DJ, PLUS a special drag performance are all on the agenda at the MFA’s First Friday tonight. PSA for Bank of America customers: You can also get into the MFA for free this weekend! Here’s how.

📚 Find your next TBR. The BPL in Copley is hosting its bi-monthly book sale on June 6 — and this is always a STEAL. Hardcovers are $2, and almost everything else is just $1 (save for a few specialty items). Name a better book deal, we dare you.

⚽ Pour one out for the jugglers. Miracle of Science is offering a $20 burger and Guinness deal to anyone doing Cambridge’s Guinness World Record attempt on June 6 for the most number of people to juggle a soccer ball.

🥵 Get hot for HIIT. Head to BREATHE in Cambridge for a heated Pride-themed pilates and strength class — perfect for your Sunday reset from post-parade festivities.

🖼️ See Beacon Hill transform into a neighborhood art gallery. Residents are opening up their courtyards on June 7 for artists to show their work, showcasing everything from paintings to ceramics to glass sculptures.

🎶 Get your Porchfest redo. If last month’s Somerville Porchfest was too … wet for your taste, head to Dorchfest on Saturday. 60+ bands across genres will be rockin’ in Ashmont-Adams, plus activities and food vendors galore.

💃 Hit the streets for this multicultural fest. Take in the food, music, and performances from cultures around the world at SomerStreets Carnaval on June 7. Expect bright colors and costumes, games, and more!

TOGETHER WITH BERKLEE

Music luminaries are coming home to Boston

🎶🎤 Berklee is making history on Sept. 19 with its inaugural Homecoming Block Party — a first-of-its-kind daylong celebration bringing together powerhouse alumni to perform in one place. Susan Tedeschi, Tiwa Savage, Fabiola Méndez, Dreion, and more music luminaries are coming home to Berklee, with additional artists to be announced leading up to the event.

Homecoming isn’t just for alumni — everyone’s invited to witness artists who’ve shaped the music industry perform at the institution that helped launch their careers. Mark Sept. 19 on your calendar, and stay tuned for the box office opening on June 16. Get a reminder by filling out the form here!

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: Suzanne Kreiter/The Boston Globe.

🚉 Commuter rail chaos countdown starts in 3, 2, 1 … From June 8 to July 12, the Fairmount, Fall River/New Bedford, Fitchburg, Framingham/Worcester, Haverhill, Needham, and Newburyport/Rockport lines will have reduced service for the World Cup. And there will be even more changes on match days. Get the full deets under each rail page. On the bright side, the Green Line E branch will be back June 6! (But Symphony Station will still be OOO.)

👀 Make way for a new downtown cultural hub. Embrace Boston, the folks behind the Boston Common Embrace statue of MLK Jr. and Coretta Scott King, just bought two buildings downtown, with plans to turn them into one “vibrant social and cultural hub.” This will be a massive 35,000-square-foot space, featuring an exhibition space, a theater, a cafe, and more. It’ll open sometime in 2030. The goal? Have a physical, permanent presence in the heart of Boston for their work in social justice and civic engagement.

🍵 Two ~green~ cafes have major updates. First, byChae, the viral matcha pop-up, is FINALLY opening a storefront on Newbury Street. It was started by a Babson College student last summer, who even took a leave of absence from school to focus on his biz. (That clearly paid off.) Then there’s Clover — remember her? Days after closing down, a mystery investor swooped in to save the local vegetarian chain’s day. Only some of its locations are set to reopen, but the owner would not spill details on which ones.

COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT

🍩 Back Door Donuts needs your votes!

Back Door Donuts is in the running AGAIN for USA TODAY’s Best Donut Shop! Last year they landed at No. 5 in the top 10, and this year, they’re going for gold. From legendary apple fritters to maple bacon and Boston cream doughnuts to cinnamon rolls, their just-baked pastries deserve the crown. Cast your vote now

ONE LAST THING

Surf and turf MORE surf

Image: Courtesy of Legal Sea Foods.

Would you pay $375 for a lobster roll? What if it’s three-feet long? Legal Sea Foods is adding a whopping four-pound lobster roll to the menu for National Lobster Day on June 15.

Why? Because shareables are in. With family-style dining being more popular, Legal’s COO Matt King wondered how he could do it with a lobster roll. His inspo? Giant party subs.

FYI, this lobster roll is prepared Maine-style with lemon mayonnaise, scallions, and celery — but King said you can ask for butter instead — and it comes with fries and coleslaw on the side. All of which can easily serve six to eight people.

This will be THE biggest lobster roll in Massachusetts, beating out Pauli’s two-foot lobster sub. And if people like it, Legal might even keep it on the menu.

— Written by Kelly Chan and Emily Schario

🦞 Thanks for reading! BTW, $375 divided between eight people is $47 per person, which is actually cheaper than Legal’s a la carte roll at $53.

Sand castles, skewers, and soccer

The Scots? Gone. Tall ships? See ya! World Cup? One foot out the door. It’s not goodbye; it’s see you later *cries*. Boston’s been having a generational run this summer, so consider this your sick weekend lineup to keep the good vibes going.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: Suzanne Kreiter/The Boston Globe.

🥬 POV: You order wine instead of a salad to avoid the poop parasite. ICYMI: There’s currently an outbreak of the cyclospora parasite known to cause *explosive* diarrhea. But luckily, Mass. has only seen a handful of cases this summer. While its source is still unclear, it’s been previously linked to contaminated food, particularly fresh produce, and water. For now, experts say to wash veggies and fruits very thoroughly (or cook them when possible), and avoid items like prewashed, bagged lettuce altogether.

🚲 Bike safety advocates are flaming City Hall. After Louisa Gag, a city transportation planner, died from a bike accident last week, residents are demanding action to make our roads safer for cyclists. TBH, advocates were already *livid* before this as the city drags its feet on several transportation safety projects and backpedals initiatives, like removing some bike lane barriers last year. Mayor Michelle Wu said they’re still investigating the details of Gag’s death to see “what needs to be done to make sure this never happens again.”

🍨 Say hello to mo’ ice cream and mo’ pizza! Popular West-coast chain Salt & Straw is opening its first Mass. location in Seaport on July 24, with fun local flavors like Boston Cream Pie and pistachio ricotta cannoli (their blackberry birthday cake is GAS). Boat buddies 4 lyfe <3

Images: Barry Chin/The Boston Globe. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

Do you want the ~house boat tour~? Imagine: A remodeled tiny home, a small fireplace, gorg wood paneling, plus every amenity you need … except it’s all on the water.

Two years ago, North Shore besties Jake Doggett and James Little bought an old 24-foot pontoon boat (which sunk in a river, btw) for $4,000, and turned it into a 100-square-foot houseboat. The kicker: They knew literally nothing about houseboats …

The whole shabang took 14 months from start to finish for a grand total of $40K (!). And like any pair of can-do 20-somethings, they created videos of the whole flipping process and went VIRAL.

Unfortunately, James took a job in Florida, so now they have it up for sale on Facebook Marketplace for a cool $140K (lowkey not bad for Mass.?). In the meantime, Jake and his girlfriend are enjoying the houseboat together in Essex Bay while they still can. <3

— Written by Kelly Chan and Emily Schario

title: Life hack: Surprise groceries?!
text:
It’s Tuesday, Boston.

🐈 This might be your cat’s claim to fame. Show your kitty off to the world at the first-ever Lower Allston Cat Stroll on Sept. 19 (basically Porchfest, but for cats). Register here!

👀 What’s on tap today:

Foliage forecast

AI-driven schools

Lizzie McGuire v. clam chowder

Up first…

FOOD & DRINK

What’s in our bag …

Images: Courtesy of Too Good To Go. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

Takeout in this economy?! How ‘bout a bag of Whole Foods leftovers for $9.99?

That’s exactly the kind of deal you’ll find on Too Good To Go, an app where users can buy surprise bags of surplus food from restaurants and markets at a *steep* discount.

But is it just another foodie Hunger Games? And are they actually any good? Here’s what we learned:

💪 Whole Foods and Caffè Nero dominate the game. These two chains take up ~half of the listings in the Boston area, according to BagRescue, a third-party tool that tracks listings and helps users reserve TGTG bags.

🍽️ Most listings cluster around the central parts of the city. Think: Back Bay, Fenway, Beacon Hill, and Downtown. Cambridge also has a good number of bags from places like Luxor Cafe and Jamie’s Ice Cream, but there are only a handful of options in the outer Boston neighborhoods like Dorchester, Roslindale, and Eastie.

💨 Popular bags can sell out FAST. Translation: You might never see an available bag from local faves like Yafa, Bakey, Iggy’s Bread, or Ba Le unless you’re on top of your notifications and have quick hands. Kelly’s pro tip for Bakey: You’ll have better luck snagging a bag at its Faneuil Hall location.

🐟 Some of the highest bags in demand? Meat and seafood from Whole Foods. And that’s across the board based on BagRescue users, according to Arash Vakil, BagRescue’s developer. But TBH, we’ve seen people on our FYP score big in their Whole Foods hauls across alllll bag types, from baked goods to produce to prepared foods (hello, two rotisserie chickens?!).

🥐 Most bags are for baked goods and groceries. Bakery items top the list around Boston, making up 30% of listings (there are tons of bread bags from places like Al’s Cafe and Bagel Guild). Fun fact: Boston has more baked and prepared items, while Cambridge actually has more grocery bags since there are more supermarket listings (i.e. Harvard Market).

🤑 You can save a real good chunk o’ change. In fact, Kelly’s biggest savings so far was actually at Bakey. She bought a bag for ~$6 and got a sesame bagel, an everything bagel, an almond babka, a date-walnut scone, AND a whole container of harissa whipped feta — a ~$25 value.

⏰ Note: Pickup times can be wonky. Be prepared to see late afternoon times (especially for cafes) and nighttime pickup windows for restaurants between 7 and 10 p.m. Sooo, not exactly a last-minute lunch solution …

🍋 Ask yourself: Is the juice worth the squeeze? You’ll always be saving a buck, but we’d recommend booking it if it’s actually convenient to grab it. Is your fridge empty? Is the spot easy to get to? But we’ll def be filing this away for move-out season …

🤔 Have more Qs? See more data here.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: John Tlumacki/The Boston Globe.

🍁 Leaf peepers, start praying for rain!!! Globe meteorologist Ken Mahan said we actually might have some vibrant foliage this fall … IF we get solid showers every week or so this month. Luckily, we just had two big storms (which also helped our drought), and with a Super El Niño a-brewin’, we should expect some more wet weather in our future. Psst! Peak colors should enter the chat around mid-October, according to this Old Farmer’s Almanac map.

📚 Chat, are these AI schools real? Yes, they are. Enter: Alpha, an AI-driven private education company that’s building 27 schools (!) across the country this year — two of which are in JP and Beacon Hill. Here’s how it works: Students spend only *two hours* on their core classes taught by AI tutors in 1:1 seshes, then work on life skills like public speaking and mental grit (see: biking across the Golden Gate Bridge) for the rest of the day. The kicker: It costs ~$60,000 a year …

🏮 The Franklin Park Zoo is getting LIT. Literally. Boston Lights is BACK, baby. In case you’re new here, the zoo hosts massive immersive lantern displays every year, and they’re *magical* (imagine: strolling through the ~glowing~ depths of the ocean and the Grand Canyon). This year will feature lanterns with South African nature inspo, like penguins and great white sharks. It’ll be up and running Thursdays through Mondays till the end of September; then you can see them *every* night from Oct. 1 to Nov. 8. Get tickets here!

👚 Coming soon: Covet in Harvard Square!!! Cambridge is *finally* getting its first Covet, opening up shop sometime this winter TBD. ICYMI, Covet was named in Boston mag’s 2026 Best of Boston for THE top place to thrift everyday essentials. In the meantime, don’t forget to bookmark Aug. 26 for their monthly $5 bin sale, where you can snag the steals of the century (we’ll never shut up about Emily’s $250 Elliatt dress).

ONE LAST THING

Lizzie McGuire v. clam chowder

Image: Evan Agostini/Invision/AP. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

Hilary Duff is officially a Masshole. At least, we’re claiming her as one after she publicly overcame her fear of clam chowder at her Mansfield concert over the weekend. (Wild sentence, we know.)

ICYMI, Hilary has been doing a silly bit on her “Lucky Me Tour” where she opens a mini fridge with surprise local foods and bevs (ex: Dirty DC in Utah, hot chicken in Nashville). This time, it was our two fave Mass. staples: clam chowder and Dunkin’ munchkins.

“I just feel like clams are little boogers or something,” she said, squirming on stage (not entirely false tbh). But she slurped a spoonful and actually LOVED the soup itself and the potatoes, calling it “wicked good.” Though she still couldn’t really get past the clams …

And for dessert, she tossed a munchkin into the air and caught it in her mouth with joy.

— Written by Kelly Chan and Emily Schario

💭 Thanks for reading! One might say, it was what dreams were made of …

🥰 Did you come to Best Day Ever? Reminder to fill out our survey here to tell us your thoughts on the event!

🏋️ The results are in: 37% of B-Siders spend under $50/month on their gym membership. But one reader shared a hack: “I used to work at Equinox, and the job came with a free membership. The job sucked, but the perks were amazing!” Can you hook us up with that referral rate??

The cat stroll’s out of the bag

Illustration: Kelly Chan.

Tired: Porchfest. Wired: Porchfest … for cats. Yep, the rumors are true. The first-ever Lower Allston Cat Stroll is happening TOMORROW, Sept. 19, when tons of kitty lovers will take to the streets for a parade-style neighborhood walk to show off their favorite felines.

Here’s what to know:

✨ It all started with a cat lover and a ~dream~. But like, kinda. Lower Allston resident Ashley Lesperance noticed a few cats perched in her neighbor’s windows while walking home one day … and the wheels started turning: She remembered Minneapolis’ wildly popular cat tour. “It looks like Somerville’s Porchfest for cats,” she said. She longed for more third spaces and community-driven events. And obviously, she loves cats (meet her furbaby Daphne).

😬 Plus, she thinks Lower Allston can get lost in the sauce. While folks might think of the neighborhood as a bunch of transient college kids, “Lower Allston, in particular, has a lot of people who’ve lived there for years,” Ashley said. And as Harvard continues to expand into the neighborhood, “there is a desire for Lower Allston to sort of hold on to what makes us Allston.”

And thus, the Lower Allston Cat Stroll was born …

📆 The day will go something like this: Everyone will gather at Smith Playground at 2 p.m. to visit local businesses like MSPCA-Angell and Molly’s Bookstore, enjoy some bevvies, and mingle with neighbors and kitties. Then, the 90-minute stroll kicks off at 2:30 p.m., when you’ll parade through the neighborhood, catching local kitties from windows, porches, and in yards. Fifty cats registered for the event, with 27 on the actual route.

🍹 And the grand finale? A Cat Stroll afterparty at Sloane’s restaurant — with cat-themed cocktails (obv) and a raffle for a $400 MSPCA cat adoption fee (aw!).

🤔 Now, let’s answer some burning Qs:

Yes, it’s free. Just show up, grab a map, and stroll!

Important: This is a dog-free event. Yes, they still love dogs, but they just want to create a safe environment for the kitties along the route. Their FAQ page politely states: “Dogs are honorary allies of the Cat Stroll and we thank them for their understanding.”

☕ Bonus: Park Bagelry, a community sponsor and partner, is offering a FREE hot or iced drip coffee with any bagel purchase now through Sept. 19. Just mention the Cat Stroll or show them this IG post at the register.

Clean Energy Center budget (to be fair, there were big federal cuts). And whether she ended working with federal immigration is … debatable.

Stop wasting time building your wardrobe piece by piece

👗 KADA is a luxury essentials brand designed for women carrying it all — careers, families, wellness, life. They get it. Founder Kassia Davis built KADA around the idea that finding elevated basics shouldn’t require endless shopping or compromise on quality. Every piece is versatile, timeless, softer than silk, and made to keep you comfy from day to evening, from brunch to beach, and from year to year. The new FW26 Woodland Collection just launched on Sept. 10, shop their new arrivals now!. Follow @wearkada, and shop here!

ONE LAST THING

Maple creemee-pedia

Image: Christian Kantosky for The Boston Globe. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

Let’s set the record straight: Maple creemees > PSLs. Yes, this silky soft-serve treat flavored with maple syrup might be a Vermont staple, but it’s been having quite the moment in Boston lately.

But, B-Side … isn’t it just soft serve??? WRONG!

The biggest difference between a creemee and classic soft serve? It has higher milkfat content AND is served a few degrees warmer, both of which give it that *extra* soft and creamy texture.

Maple creemees have been a Vermont mainstay since the 80s, but they’ve slowly made their way to Boston (finally).

You can find them at Vinal General Store, Madeleine’s Candy Shop, and Momma’s Grocery + Wine (which sells them year-round!).

But if you’re ever driving up to Vermont … Morse Farm Maple Sugarworks in Montpelier is ELITE.

— Written by Kelly Chan and Emily Schario

title: We have a present for you!
text:
Happy Friday, Boston!

🤑 Ever wonder what a $17 million apartment looks like? Well … take a peek inside this recently sold Beacon Hill brownstone and see!

🥳 HBD to B-Side Members Alex Issokson and Abby Sweeney! We wish we could give you each a $17 million brownstone … but we hope you liked the pics. <3

👀What’s on tap today:

Good luck, Red Liners

The price of living in Boston

A $48 pizza …

Up first…

CARE PACKAGE

Your spring starter pack

Illustration: Gia Orsino

We made it through yet another cold, dark winter! And for that, you deserve a little treat …

We’re back with another B-Side Care Package, a.k.a. our roundup of media, things to do, food, and everything else that we (and our pals!) have been loving lately:

🥪 Spice up your spring eats. As the weather warms, most people default to lobster rolls, ice cream, and hot dogs, but not Key Henson (a.k.a. @wannabestayathomedad). His fav bite this season is a crispy red snapper sandwich from Juicy Jay’s inside Kendall Square’s Eastern Edge Food Hall. Think: Golden crunch, perfectly flaky fish, and a cool, refreshing coleslaw tying it all together.

📺 Learn about the world through reality TV. Further proof of Emily’s take that watching reality TV is basically modern-day anthropology: TikToker @soberchampagne, who explains world events using “Vanderpump Rules.” Turns out, it’s a lot easier to understand the rise and fall of the Roman Empire in the context of Scandoval.

🦉 Go on a woodcock walk. Every year from March to May, Gia joins the many birders and non-birders who gather to watch American Woodcocks do their silly little mating dance, including right here in Boston. As someone dating a birder, she wouldn’t recommend just any bird excursion, but this one is equal parts magical and absurd. Try this Woodcock Watch at the Boston Nature Center.

👭 Dive into a platonic love story. Need a spring read? “Love by the Book” by Jessica George comes recommended by Annie Jonas of Boston.com’s book club newsletter. It follows two 30-something women finding each other as their old support systems fall apart. Jonas said it’s a funny, tender, and deeply honest read about outgrowing friendships — and choosing new ones.

📚 Speaking of books … read one outside. For Globe Living/Arts correspondent Annie Sarlin, spring = outdoor reading season. Her go-to spot: Trident Booksellers & Cafe. She’ll browse their shelves for her next read, then grab a table outside to soak up the sunshine. Bonus points if you grab coffee or a treat (especially the lemon ricotta-stuffed french toast).

🥾 Take a hike! One of Walking City Trails creator Miles Howard‘s favorite spring rituals is a trek across Middlesex Fells’ Cross Fells Trail. Though it’s a 10-minute walk from Oak Grove, the infinite trees and great lookout points feel “a world apart from Greater Boston,” he said. Plus, when you get to the other end, you can catch a bus to Medford Center and refuel with a giant torta from Tenoch.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: Craig F. Walker/The Boston Globe

🚇 Red Liners, it’s service change szn. Remember those nightly service changes we told you about back in February? We have an update! From now through approximately April 9, Braintree branch riders will need to transfer to Alewife-Ashmont trains for service beyond JFK/UMass after 8 p.m. Then, it’ll flip, and Ashmont riders will need to transfer to Alewife-Braintree trains through around April 26. Plus, you can expect longer travel times between Ashmont/Braintree and JFK/UMass and reduced train frequency the whole time. Good luck, babe!

🍏 Boston teachers have a budget problem. The Boston Teachers Union and education advocates are fighting proposed cuts that would nix 300 to 400 jobs across city schools in the upcoming city budget. BPS officials say the cuts are necessary considering the district’s enrollment decline of about 3,000 students since the 2024-25 school year — in part thanks to President Trump’s immigration crackdown. But advocates are asking for Wu and the City Council to ward off cuts by investing an additional 1% of the city’s budget (or $48 million) in the schools.

💸 How much do you need to earn to live comfortably in Boston? $139,776 a year, according to a new study by SmartAsset. Apparently, that’s how much a Bostonian needs to follow a true 50/30/20 budget — spending 50% of your income on necessities, 30% on wants, and 20% on savings. It’s also ~$42,000 more than Boston’s median household income of $97,791, and an increase of ~$6,000 over last year, putting Boston sixth on the list overall behind NYC and several cities in California. *Sobs*

🤤 Ballin’ on a budget? Head to Malden! Boston.com’s affordable eats series took the Orange Line up to Malden, rounding up the city’s best bites under $20. On the menu: $15 birria tacos at Caliente Mexican Grill, a super beef-sized roast beef sandwich for $13.50 at Fresco’s Roast Beef & Seafood, and enough dim sum to leave with plenty of leftovers at Sun Kong (prices vary). Ready to dig in? You can check out all of Malden’s cheap eats here.

THINGS TO DO

Weekend plans

🛍️ Go vintage or go home. Between Small Mart’s Davis Square night market on March 27 and Brighton Bazaar’s Spring Market on March 29, there will be plenty of vintage, vinyl, and art to shop.

🥣 Slurp soup for a good cause. On March 28, the Empty Bowls Project will serve up hot soup in stunning hand-crafted bowls, and proceeds go toward combatting hunger and homelessness. There are still a few seats left!

🖤 Show your mom it’s not just a phase. Emo Night Brooklyn is coming to Brighton Music Hall on March 28 for a night of big music, big mosh pits, and big feelings.

🍵 Join the matcha madness. On March 29, Hue Boston will be taken over by Matcha Madness: a two-story celebration of matcha and coffee with music, brunch, and lots of caffeine.

🙋‍♀️ Learn from some boss babes. Northeastern’s annual WISE Summit is back on March 28 with speakers, workshops, and fireside chats to help women grow a brand, company, or career.

🎥 Watch Harry meet Sally. The iconic romcom is playing for free at Lamplighter Brewing on March 29. There will be brews, popcorn, and pizza for purchase.

🚶‍♀️Walk with the gals. Volo and Boston Girls Who Walk are teaming up for a Women’s History Month Walk on March 29. The 2.5-mile stroll will end with complimentary apps at 261, the Envoy’s women’s sports-themed pop-up.

✏️ Doodle the day away. The Foundry’s pop-up Dar Cafe is hosting a cozy sketch and doodle meetup on March 29. Pro tip: Get the cherry blossom matcha!

ONE LAST THING

Boston’s bougiest pizza

Illustration: Gia Orsino

You’ve heard of $1 pizza. Now, allow us to introduce … $48 pizza. Meet La Zarina, the bougiest pie in Boston from the Pru’s new pizzeria, CeCarré.

If you’re thinking: What is this pizza made of? Gold? Yes it is. The pie is literally topped with edible 23-karat gold, plus caviar, mozzarella, pecorino, potatoes, gruyère, crème fraîche, and chives. At least you’ll get your money’s worth.

CeCarré’s full pies have about four large slices each, but if you’re not willing to shell out, you can also get a half La Zarina for $24, or just a slice for $12. And for those of us who prefer their pies without gold and caviar, a CeCarré Classic, with mozz, pecorino, tomato sauce, and parmigiano will run you $22.

Here’s a peek at the golden pie.

— Written by Gia Orsino

title: Moving in Boston costs HOW much?
text:
It’s Thursday, Boston.

Lunar eclipse tonight!!

MONEY SMARTER, NOT HARDER

How to save some dough on Sept. 1

Photo illustration: Luis G. Rendon/The Boston Globe; Adobe. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

Today’s top story is from Boston Globe housing reporter Andrew Brinker, who just so happens to be moving! How meta. So as the Sept. 1 shuffle approaches, he’s sharing his tips for staying sane and keeping your bank account stacked.

Moving is a huge hassle. Take it from me. It’s also not so unusual to fork over up-front move-in costs over $10,000. Yes, I typed the correct number of zeros.

So if your head is spinning ahead of the big move, here’s how to keep your $$$ ducks in a row:

📅 Let’s state the obvious: Start squirreling away cash yesterday. Some 60% of families in Greater Boston don’t have enough cash on hand to cover up-front move-in costs. So the more of your move you can pay for out of pocket, the better. The last thing you want is credit card debt burning a hole in your pocket. And remember: Your security deposit, first, and last month’s rent will come back to you eventually. <3

🚚 And then there’s the *literal* cost of moving. Hiring movers? If you’re trekking a relatively short distance (i.e., within Boston, or from Dorchester to Cambridge), plan to spend anywhere from $500 to a few Gs, depending on how much stuff you have.

🤔 Should I get renters insurance? It’s not a bad idea. Renters insurance is not legally required in Mass., however … if something were to happen to your building — a fire, flooding, or theft — your landlord is generally not liable for covering the costs of your lost belongings. Plus, renters insurance is relatively cheap — think $10-30 a month. So if you want peace of mind that your designer rug or custom-built computer will be protected, it may be worth considering.

📮 Don’t forget: Change! Your! Address! Just because a bill doesn’t reach you doesn’t mean it’s not due. Here’s what I’d do:

Submit a formal change of address with the U.S. Postal Service by filling out an easy form online (ideally two weeks before you move, but ya know … here we are).

Notify any major institutions that send you mail — think banks, your employer, insurance companies. Most places let you do this online, too.

Get in touch with whoever is taking over your lease in case they accidentally end up with some of your mail.

🏆 The ultimate pro tip? Don’t move on Sept. 1. Yes, I know, it’s unavoidable for many, but it’s also the best way to dodge the chaos. Roughly two-thirds of all of the leases in Boston turn over that day, which is when moving costs are at their absolute peak. Even a week on either side of Sept. 1 will typically turn up slightly discounted prices for movers, U-Hauls, you name it.

🎄 And as always … A Merry Allston Christmas to all, and to all a good night.

CITY

Quick & dirty headlines

Image: Robert F. Bukaty/AP, File.

🌒 We’re ~over the moon~ about this eclipse. Pour another cup o’ joe tonight, ‘cause we’re expecting a sick partial lunar eclipse — which should lowkey be much cooler than this month’s solar eclipse, as long as there’s a break in the clouds. The lunar eclipse will start around 9:30 p.m. and peak just past midnight when just a sliver of the moon will be illuminated and 96% will have a reddish-copper glow. And unlike with the solar eclipse, you can stare at this one with your bare eyes.

♻️ Cambridge laid down new zero-waste rules. Starting Feb. 3, 2027, a few changes take effect: 1. Residential and commercial buildings will have to separate food waste from the regular trash (there will be a separate food waste collection). 2. Plastic bags won’t be available at checkout, like at all. 3. Local businesses will give napkins, utensils, and condiments only upon request. 4. Property managers will have to submit zero waste plans for their buildings. 5. Trash bins need to be labeled, closed, and replaced if they’re damaged.

🥤 Greater Boston’s been watching too much Mormon reality TV. Because Swig is officially planting roots here. The popular Utah-based dirty soda brand is opening up SIX spots in the region, with the first in early 2027 (locations TBD). For dirty soda virgins: It’s basically a combo of soda + cream + sweet syrups. Dunkin’ recently tried to hop on the dirty soda craze … but it got mixed reviews from locals. But we do like the sound of a DDC (dirty Diet Coke).

👅 Add these bites to your summer bucket list before the season ends. Before you go full PSL, Globe food critic Devra First gave us her top 10 list of summer treats to indulge in. Want a beach vibe? Order a pupu platter and a mai tai at Kowloon Tiki on the Beach — it’s B-Side Certified! Craving tacos? Go to Taqueria Jalisco in Eastie (the birria tacos are BEYOND). For dessert, take the short walk to Slush King for their creamy homemade gelato. Need something green? Fallow Kin’s and Oleana’s veg-forward menus are your girls.

COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT

🍕 Boston’s oldest pizzeria just turned 100

Did you know Regina Pizzeria was Boston’s first-ever pizza parlor?! Founded in 1926 in the North End, Regina’s is still cookin’ their famous thin-crust pies in their OG brick oven, and they’ve kept the same delish formula ever since. Celebrate their 100th birthday at any of their locations!

ONE LAST THING

Twinned in Tartan

Image: Courtesy of Buchanan Galleries. Illustration: Kelly Chan.

Fit Kilt check! Our Scottish sisters have released two new tartan designs honoring our cities’ kindred spirits, and you’re gonna wanna see them.

The first one, launched by Glasgow shopping center Buchanan Galleries, is called “Twinned in Tartan,” an ocean blue pattern with hints of red, yellow, and green. Fun fact: This kilt will be presented for “Tartan Day” in April, when Boston and Glasgow officially celebrate their partnership.

The other tartan, from the North East Tartan Army, has been dubbed “New Scotland Massachusetts.” It’s got a deep, dark navy blue with bright red and white stripes (yes, it’s kind of giving Catholic school uniform lol).

The best part? The North East folks plan to bring a few extra kilts to Boston this fall, AND we should see Buchanan’s design here sometime next year.

— Written by Kelly Chan and Emily Schario

title: The good news stories you might've missed this month
text:
It’s Monday, Boston.
